claims.text: The as-cast Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni EHEA has a continuous, coarse dual-phase lamellar microstructure that exhibits low room-temperature ductility and catastrophic interfacial cracking.
Severe plastic deformation followed by controlled annealing will transform the continuous lamellae into a patterned heterogeneous microstructure.
The resulting microstructure will contain alternating ultra-fine-grained and coarse-grained regions, or fragmented lamellae with high-angle boundaries.
Severe deformation introduces a high dislocation density and breaks up the lamellae.
Annealing at 800–1000 °C for 10–60 minutes will induce phase-selective recrystallization in which the softer phase becomes ultra-fine grained while the harder phase remains coarse or fragmented.
The proposed mechanical response is to be evaluated by room-temperature uniaxial tension at a strain rate of 1 × 10^-3 s^-1.
High-pressure torsion should be performed at a pressure greater than 1 GPa.
High-angle boundaries and phase-selectively refined regions will act as barriers to crack propagation.
A heterogeneous grain-size distribution creates geometrically necessary dislocations that generate back stresses.
Back-stress hardening delays necking and promotes uniform plasticity.
Fragmenting continuous lamellar interfaces will force cracks to deflect or arrest at ultra-fine-grained region boundaries.
The treated alloy will attain a uniform elongation greater than 20%.
The as-cast Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni baseline has less than 10% elongation.
The treated alloy will maintain or increase its ultimate tensile strength to greater than 1.5 GPa.
Ultra-fine-grain Hall–Petch strengthening and back-stress hardening will be responsible for maintaining or increasing the strength.
The fracture mode will change from interfacial cleavage to ductile micro-void coalescence.
The treatment will reduce microcrack density by at least 50% relative to the baseline.
Annealing below 800 °C will not produce sufficient recrystallization.
Annealing above 1000 °C will cause excessive grain growth or phase dissolution and produce a coarse homogeneous structure.
A deformation reduction greater than 60% is required to break the lamellae.

contradictions.description: The proposed treatment permits ordinary multi-pass rolling at standard pressure as an alternative to high-pressure torsion, but the falsification rule frames extreme pressure as necessary. Thus extreme pressure is not consistently defined as an essential intervention.

The HITMT and HIP sets differ in deformation mode, accumulated strain, annealing duration, and pressure, so their comparison does not isolate extreme pressure. Equal or superior HIP performance would not by itself distinguish pressure effects from these other processing differences.
